definitions.explanation: A contest whose outcome settles everything, leaving no second chance for the loser. Literally 'the dividing point of the realm', from the historical struggles that decided who would rule Japan. Used with の before the noun it modifies.

examples.japanese: {天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{戦|たたか}い→戦い：02070_tatakai⟧だ。
{明日|あす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Tomorrow's match will be the make-or-break one.

examples.japanese: {関|せき}ヶ{原|はら}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{戦|たたか}い→戦い：02070_tatakai⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Sekigahara is known as the battle that decided the fate of the country.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{取|と}れる→取れる：02376_toreru⟧⟦かどうか→かどうか：28299_kadouka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{我|わ}が{社|しゃ}⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧{天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{勝負|しょうぶ}→勝負：01437_shoubu⟧だ。
examples.english: Whether we land this contract is a make-or-break fight for our company.

notes:
Nearly always used attributively with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧, above all in the set phrase {天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{戦|たたか}い→戦い：02070_tatakai⟧. The historical reference point is the Battle of Sekigahara (1600), which decided who would rule Japan; modern uses transfer that weight to elections, sports finals, and business deals, often with a touch of deliberate grandiosity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{戦|たたか}い→戦い：02070_tatakai⟧: the decisive battle
- {天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一戦|いっせん}→一戦：16246_issen⟧: the deciding match
- {天下分|てんかわ}け{目|め}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{勝負|しょうぶ}→勝負：01437_shoubu⟧: a make-or-break contest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{決戦|けっせん}→決戦：13253_kessen⟧: decisive battle — plainer and more neutral, no historical flavor
- ⟦{正念場|しょうねんば}→正念場：13193_shounenba⟧: crucial moment — a testing phase one must get through, not a contest between two sides
